newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica says suit is "short on reality".
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica says suit is "short on reality".

text.p: BankAmerica Corp said claims in a lawsuit launched by the city of San Francisco relating to alleged mishandling of municipal bond funds are short on reality and the bank had a refund project underway before the city raised the issue.

"If you strip away the rhetoric and bring both the allegations and the damage estimates down to earth, what really happened is that the bank's corporate trust department unintentionally overcharged the city for trust services and retained some funds that should have been returned to the city or escheated (return unclaimed funds) to the state," said James Roethe, Bank of America's General Counsel in statement.
Earlier, San Francisco sued Bank of America for more than $12 million, alleging the bank, acting as a trustee, mishandled municipal bond funds.
The bonds were issued by the city, the San Francisco School District, the San Francisco Housing Authority and the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency.
BankAmerica said the allegations relate to the Institutional Trust Department, which it sold in 1995.

"The bank discovered the overcharge errors on its own and voluntarily refunded over $5 million to its customers," Roethe said. The bank believes the refunds it has already made compensate the city fully for any overcharges.
"Even so, we stand ready to reimburse the city further for any additional claims that they can substantiate," Roethe said.
The bank reiterated that its exposure to the city's claims would not be material, despite the City Attorney's inference.
Roethe said the city's claims that BofA withheld funds that should have been returned to the city, the state, or other state agencies, need to be resolved at the state level.
It said it is working with the state and offered to submit to an outside audit to determine what it owes.
The city also claims that Bank of America caused it to suffer investment losses by improperly investing funds in the trust accounts through a sweep mechanism.
